properties.name: Advice
properties.location: Murray River downstream of Tocumwal to Barham
properties.webBody:
This Minor Flood Warning is being issued for the Murray River downstream of Tocumwal to Barham.

  • Upstream flows from the Murray River, combined with flood waters from the Goulburn River, are causing minor flooding along the Murray River at Barham. 
  • River levels are expected to remain around the minor flood level into early September as flood waters continue to arrive from upstream.
  • Minor flooding is occurring at Barham.
  • The Murray River at Barham is currently at 5.55m and steady, just above the minor flood level (5.50m). 
  • The Murray River at Barham is likely to remain around the minor flood level into early September.
Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and remain alert.
What you should do: 
  • Be prepared to act if your situation changes.
  • Stay informed by listening to emergency broadcasters and monitoring warnings. 
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never drive, walk or ride through floodwater. 
  • Monitor weather forecasts and river levels. Go to www.bom.gov.au/vic/warnings/
Impacts in your area: 
  • High river levels and potential flooding in areas close to rivers and streams.
  • Camping grounds may be flooded.
  • Boating in floodwaters is dangerous due to debris, submerged trees and other hidden dangers.
This message was issued by State Emergency Service.

The next update is expected by 31/08/2026 01:30 pm or as the situation changes.

Use multiple sources to stay informed:
  • www.emergency.vic.gov.au
  • VicEmergency Hotline - freecall 1800 226 226
  • VicEmergency app
  • Facebook
  • Tune in to ABC Local Radio, commercial and designated community radio stations, or News24 TV.
Accessibility: 
The following services can help you, or someone you know, access information during an emergency. 
  • To access this information in other languages, call the Translating and Interpreting Service on 131 450 (freecall) and ask them to call VicEmergency Hotline. 
  • If you are deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech/communication impairment, contact the National Relay Service and ask them to call the VicEmergency Hotline.

properties.location: Kiewa River downstream of Mongans Bridge
properties.webBody:
This is a Final Minor Flood Warning for Kiewa River downstream of Mongans Bridge. 
  • Minor flooding has eased along the Kiewa River at Bandiana.
  • The Kiewa River at Bandiana is currently at 2.66 meters and falling, below the minor flood level. 
  • The Kiewa River at Bandiana is expected to remain below the minor flood level 2.80 meters.
The threat of flooding is reduced. Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and beware of hazards remaining in the warning area.
What you should do:
  • Be prepared to act if your situation changes.
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never enter floodwater.
If your home or business has been flooded:
  • Check for building damage before you enter.
  • Have all electrical and gas equipment professionally tested before use.
  • Clean and dry out the building as soon as possible.
Call Triple Zero (000) in a life threatening emergency. For emergency assistance from the SES call 132 500.
Impacts in your area: 
  • Damage to roads and buildings caused by flooding may still exist in your area. 
This message was issued by State Emergency Service.

This will be the last warning for this flood.

properties.name: Advice
properties.location: Avoca River downstream of Charlton Town
properties.webBody:
This Minor Flood Warning is being issued for the Avoca River downstream of Charlton Town.

  • Minor flooding is occurring at Quambatook.
  • The Avoca River at Quambatook is currently at 2.01m and steady, above the minor flood level (2.00m). 
  • The Avoca River at Quambatook is likely to peak near 2.10m overnight Monday into Tuesday, with minor flooding.
  • This is an update, replacing the Advice message issued at 11:12am on Sunday 30 August.
Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and remain alert.
What you should do: 
  • Be prepared to act if your situation changes.
  • Drivers must be alert to water over roads, especially overnight when visibility is poor.
  • Do not enter flooded areas. Turn around and find a safe alternative route.
  • Never drive, walk or ride through floodwater.
  • Be aware of road hazards including mud, debris and damaged roads or bridges.
Impacts in your area: 
  • Some local roads are closed or have speed restrictions. Drivers must follow diversions. For more information on road closures visit the VicTraffic website.
  • Flooding of farmland downstream of Glenloth around Bunguluke and Ninyeunook, and inundation of local roads such as Jeruk River Road North and Ninyeunook Road.
  • Floodwaters may persist for several days as they move through the floodplain.
  • High river levels and potential flooding in areas close to rivers and streams.
This message was issued by State Emergency Service.

The next update is expected by 01/09/2026 01:00 pm or as the situation changes.

  • www.emergency.vic.gov.au
  • VicEmergency Hotline - freecall 1800 226 226
